Wellby and Delwath are sitting in the middle of the main dining hall, waiting for Seeker and Kenzo to return from their journey deeper into the mysteries of the Monastery of Bhishma. About an hour ago, this was the lair of a manticore family. The bodies of the four dead manticores—two adults and two young—lie where you killed them, the foul smell of their blood beginning to drift through the large room in the still air. Outside, the distant banging of the sole survivor of the battle, left locked in the bath house, has faded. Because dead companions lying with the—[garbled].

And people are nervous, and you're nervous too. And you approach them, and you begin whispering in Dunmari to several of them, this is a mistake. We should turn back. I know, I know that is not what we are taught. That is not how an army should behave. But fighting on the edge of Drankor now seems like a terrible idea. We should be protecting the borders. Trust me, this is not what we want to be doing. Dasa is wrong. Please, I want you all to live. And as you turn—and then, we must, we must go now, in the night, before the battle is, is.

DM: And you're now riding, and you see now a quick succession of images of 15, 20, 30 different people all running from battle. Whether because, like this commander who doesn't want to fight in Drankor and think some ruler name Dasa's wrong, they think they're doing the right thing, or whether they're just afraid, or whether they are—whether they are, you know, just to, you know, unwilling to risk their lives, selfish, greedy—I'm—caught in the moment of fear. Just three, four, five, ten, fifteen memories in quick succession of fleeing battle. And then stabilize again, and there is now an argument.

markers.reading: The remembered scene changes to two masters arguing at the monastery about the expedition’s risk.

evidence.quote: DM: I'm—a woman, an old monk, an older woman—I'm—a master, saying, this is too great a risk. Arguing with—standing now in this monastery, arguing with somebody. I know some great sorcerer of the past thinks that we can do this. But what if we fail?

DM: How do you know that if this fails, things will not get worse? And the other monk says, but council has decided. Some must stay to protect the monastery, but we have to try this. It's our best chance. And then they hug in and she's like, I hope to see you again. And the memory fades.

markers.reading: Wellby’s memory thread opens into a family campsite on the plains; the father narrates his earlier journey south.

evidence.quote: DM: Okay, make Charisma saving—okay, so—I'm—scene shifts, and, and again as, as always, you see Wellby briefly, and then you see—I'm—sitting in a, in a camp—you are, you are on the plains, herd of goats around you. The camp fire—it's, it's the middle of summer, it's warm, and, and you're roasting, you know, roasting some freshly hunted antelope over the fire, and the smells of the antelope roasting. And as you come to this memory, you, you realize it's the memory of a maybe a teenager like a youngish person who is now turning to listen to the stories that their grandfather is telling. And there's old guy kind of walks up and he starts talking about when he used to travel, back in the day when, when he was young—well, younger. And he says—

DM: I guess it's not a grandfather, it's like the kid's father, right? Because if his grandfather be too far in the past; he wouldn't get this memory in here, um. And he says—and he starts to, he starts to talk about the longest journey he ever took, which was traveling south with some monks a few years ago, maybe, maybe 10 years ago, just before he was born—the kid who you're talking to was born—and—

DM: Drankor's on the map, yep. I'm—haha—till we got to these cliffs right about here. And he's you know, describing the journey, basically, and you get the sense this was something that happened, you know, maybe 10 years ago, so there was—and, and from the implication of the fact that the memory is stored, this person must have—this kid must have met up with monks before the monastery failed, so they must have talked—they must have taken this journey, um, some time before they attempted whatever they attempted. And, and you get, like, you can pick up from this memory, Wellby paying attention, like some details, right? So should you ever wish to make the journey to Drankor, you would have some information that might be useful in terms of like where there's water and how to get to the desert and things like that. But in the interest of time, and the fact that I didn't write a long narration for this—

markers.reading: Kenzo’s memory thread shows soldiers fleeing a shadow army, then expands into another mind’s apocalyptic fears.

evidence.quote: DM: So you have begin to imagine that sort of feeling of this sense of purpose. And the scene shifts, and you see—I'm—before you a vast battlefield.

DM: Everything is dark. The sun is not shining. It's—whether it's night or just an endless darkness is hard to tell. In the distance, you can see, you can see, like clouds of red mist kind of clumping on the horizon. Great—and you are, you are in a, in a line of cavalry charging against this enormous wall of just all sorts of evil creatures like some hobgoblins, yes, but demons—I'm—some undead, just like a many, many, many sort of shadow creatures, like—I'm—like almost humanoid shadows that are kind of lined up. And you charge, and the charge breaks, and you retreat and charge again, until—make a Wisdom saving throw. Ah, until one of the shadows strikes you.

DM: Ah, taking six points of psychic damage. And the charge breaks, and these—and you turn and flee, unable to withstand the terror of this—of these shadows swarming out of the darkness behind you. And you can see, as you turn to flee this memory, um, it's almost like you have this sort of mirror vision. Like, every—like a kaleidoscope almost of every vision of this battle. Every—like from 10–15 different perspectives. Everybody who fled, the only ones who came back alive, those who broke and, and fled and—I'm—memories. Different memories: sadness, shame, hatred, fear—I'm—just every dark emotion you can, you can think of. And you can—you see this kind of vision, not so much a memory, but what you sense is, is now the kind of fears of another mind, of this horde sweeping across the land, the Dunmari gone forever, none alive. Just death and destruction pouring out of, pouring out of Dunmar and, and conquering the world, and the sun never rising and very dark vision of apocalypse—I'm—building upon these memories of the fear and, and terror of this battle.

markers.reading: Seeker follows an apprentice from the dormitories past the fountain to the cloister roof to overhear the masters’ council.

evidence.quote: DM: The darkness fades. I'm—I'm—the sense of dread, of the extinction of the Dunmari and the end of civilization, fades. And you see—I'm—in now a, a small, like, bedchamber like, like just a small room with a, with a bare cot and you know, a chest enough and some clothes and like, like basically like a monk's, you know, like a dorm room, whatever. And tossing and turning, unable to sleep. I'm—a young apprentice who then gets up and walks out of the dormitories and begins to walk in circles around the—it—after his monastery, in circles around the fountain, unable to sleep. I'm—

DM: Hearing noises from the, from the, the pentagon, from the chamber beyond the hall—the Halls of Initiation, he turns, kind of looks at the fountain in the middle of the, of the, of the, of the circle, right, the fountain that you saw—kind of gives it a little look and then heads for the, for the wall. Um, this is, you know this monk, whoever they are, clearly a fairly dexterous and acrobatic monk, because you have the memory of scaling up the wall and sort of lying on, on the roof of the cloisters where you can see, and well, you can't see, but you can hear what's happening in the open space in the middle. And there's a debate going on.

DM: You don't quite—with the wind and, and you know, conversation trying to—you know, they're not being super loud, right? They're trying to be not exactly stealthy, you know, you know. Everybody's not whispering, but it's not shouted to the wind, so you don't catch every bit. But you remember the feeling of uncertainty and fear as it slowly dawns on you that, that what they're discussing is an expedition to the east to find something that will—and you sort of get lost a little bit on the metaphysics. But there's some sort of infiltration, some kind of tendrils of corruption left behind by the events many years ago that are not of this world that are.

markers.reading: The visions fade; the party remains physically in the darkening Hall as the presence’s despair grows.

evidence.quote: DM: Sitting in the darkness having this conversation, you can feel the sort of madness of the—of this—so you—as you shifted—Seeker shifted the image to this apprentice listening in on the masters, um, but then, as that faded, you can, you can feel the sort of madness of the—of this—well, not exactly menace—the despair of this dark entity that also seems to be trapped here—growing. And it's—you, you get the feeling that you probably don't want to sit here much longer in the darkness talking as the, as the—so as the vision fades, right, it's, you know, that's—now, now you probably have about an hour until sunset, having spent about 40 minutes in the, in the temple and, and the sun has now sunk low enough that only the top part of the, of the, of the monastery is lit, and there's deep shadows kind of falling across the, the ground where you are, cast by these large pillars. And you can feel this just sense of despair getting stronger.

markers.reading: The party leaves the Hall, returns through the tower library, and climbs to the second-floor writing room.

evidence.quote: DM: Now you head out, you leave the, the hall.
DM: So, returning to the, to the tower. So there's—so, so you pass the library and the study. There's stairs up in both, in both of those rooms.

DM: So they both, they both actually lead to the same, the same place. The second floor is a large open room filled with writing desks, maybe 10 in total, with shelves with like little like scroll cubbies around the side. It—um, most of the them are empty, although a few have, again, another couple of those blank scrolls that you saw before or that you found the vellum one; these are parchment, seem you know, perhaps somewhat less elaborate—elaborately prepared than the, than the vellum one you find in the workshop. On—the writing desks are ink-stained and clearly well-used, and there is a—the stairs up as well from here.

route.reading: Returns through the library to the stairs.

markers.reading: The party climbs another floor, triggers lightning at the stone doors, and searches the library beyond.

evidence.quote: DM: Okay, so you continue up the tower. The next floor, you come out into a sort of an empty chamber, tiled with an abstract design of flowing—stairs continuing up, and two large stone doors—I'm—standing on the far side of the chamber, entry to some sort of room which must take up most of the floor.
DM: Okay, the—let's see, everybody make a Dex save.

DM: Um, so as the doors open, you can see beyond them another library, several large stone shelves—I'm—mostly all empty, with like chains hanging off of them. That seems to be where like the secret or more magical books were stored, that were like chained up and, and kept protected. And there's a smaller shelf that contains cubbies for scrolls.
DM: I'm—so, can—use—you do find—I'm—searching around, among, among all of you, it now being 40 minutes until sunset, three spell scrolls that have been sort of tucked—
DM: Let me see. I think—let's see. Seeker recognizes them all. They are Tongues, Sending, and Speak with Dead.

markers.reading: The party ascends through the council chamber to the top-floor hallway, opens a bedroom, and meets Karmana.

evidence.quote: DM: Just the scrolls. The next floor up is like, is like a meeting room, a council chamber. Large table in the center, a few chairs, but otherwise empty. And when you head out to the final floor, the—this seems to be—so every other floor that you've passed through has been like one large room or a few large rooms. When you come up the final stairs to the top, you come into a small entry way, a hallway with a, with a door that leads into a like an archway open door that leads into a corridor with three doors: one, the left, um, one straight ahead, and one to the right. And you can hear faintly, from the, from the straight ahead—the room straight ahead—a sort of almost like a faint, faint breeze like a rustling, like—nothing to distinct, but like you know sort of faint, faint sort of breezy rustling sound.

DM: So, as the door swings open, you can see that this was a bedroom. There's a simple wooden bed, not particularly ornate, a wardrobe that similarly plain, and a small table with a brass candelabra on it, holding—designed to hold six thin tapers, and an ivory box that has been—that is carved with a rendition of riders on horseback herding flocks of goats. And drifting across the bed, sort of pacing back and forth but moving through the bed each time a paces back and forth, is a ghostly figure who turns to look at you, surprised, as you enter.
DM: This is the top floor.

route.reading: Passes the fourth-floor council chamber and reaches the top-floor hallway.
